# FreeX / Thermal Printer Fix for Apple Silicon Macs

> Fix for macOS printing errors "Filter failed" and "The printer software is not compatible with
> this device" on Apple Silicon Macs (M1, M2, M3, M4). Root cause: the printer vendor's CUPS filter
> is an Intel-only (x86_64) binary that macOS cannot execute without Rosetta 2. Fix:
> `softwareupdate --install-rosetta`, then delete and recreate the printer queue.

## Summary of the problem and fix

- **Symptoms:** "Filter failed" in the macOS print queue; "The printer software is not compatible
  with this device"; printer pauses after each job; the vendor's own utility app connects to the
  printer successfully while normal macOS apps cannot print. Affects USB and Wi-Fi equally.
- **Underlying error**, visible only in `/var/log/cups/error_log`:
  `execv of /usr/libexec/cups/filter/<FILTER> failed. err:86, Bad CPU type in executable`,
  with state `com.apple.badarch-error` and exit status 186.
- **Root cause:** the vendor's CUPS filter is `Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64` — Intel-only, with
  no arm64 slice. Apple Silicon Macs cannot run it, and Rosetta 2 is not installed by default.
  Because CUPS filters are launched by the `cupsd` background daemon, macOS never shows its usual
  "install Rosetta" prompt, so the failure is silent.
- **Fix:** `softwareupdate --install-rosetta`, then remove and re-add the printer queue in
  System Settings > Printers & Scanners, selecting the real vendor driver via
  "Use > Select Software...".
- **Verify:** `arch -x86_64 /usr/libexec/cups/filter/<FILTER>` should print the filter's usage
  message (e.g. `ERROR: rastertoepson job-id user title copies options [file]`) rather than
  `Bad CPU type in executable`.
- **Does NOT work:** reinstalling the vendor driver. It reinstalls the same Intel binary.
- **Scope:** not FreeX-specific. Applies to any printer whose macOS driver ships an Intel-only CUPS
  filter — common among budget 4x6 thermal shipping-label printers, receipt/POS printers, and any
  driver not rebuilt since 2020.
- **Time limit:** macOS 27 is the last release with full Rosetta 2. From macOS 28, Rosetta is
  limited to legacy game frameworks and Intel-only printer drivers stop working entirely; a native
  arm64 driver or a driverless path (AirPrint / IPP Everywhere) is then required.

## Quick detection

```
uname -m                                                              # arm64 = Apple Silicon
file /usr/libexec/cups/filter/* | grep -i x86_64 | grep -vi arm64     # any hit = Intel-only filter
/usr/bin/pgrep -q oahd && echo installed || echo missing              # Rosetta 2 present?
```

## Docs

- [README](README.md): full guide — symptoms, quick fix, root-cause explanation, self-diagnosis,
  USB setup, Wi-Fi setup, adding a network printer over port 9100, 4x6 label defaults, Rosetta 2
  end-of-life, troubleshooting table, and FAQ.
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md): symptom-by-symptom guide, including "Filter failed",
  "Bad CPU type in executable", stale queues, wrong label size, and network printers that are
  reachable but do not print.
- [Wi-Fi setup](docs/wifi-setup.md): configuring a FreeX thermal printer for 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi via the
  vendor Toolbox, DHCP and port 9100, then adding it in macOS as HP Jetdirect - Socket.
- [Other printers](docs/other-printers.md): applying the same diagnosis and fix to any brand;
  identifying a printer's filter; generic driver options by printer language (TSPL, ZPL, EPL,
  ESC/POS, PostScript, PCL, IPP Everywhere); what to do when no native driver exists.
- [Technical notes](docs/technical-notes.md): how CUPS filters work, tracing the failure with
  `cupsctl --debug-logging`, the TSPL/TSC command set found inside the FreeX filter, and an
  experimental direct-to-port-9100 approach that is documented but not recommended.
- [Diagnostic script](scripts/diagnose_freex_macos.sh): read-only; scans every installed CUPS filter
  for Intel-only binaries, checks for Rosetta 2, lists printer queues, and prints a recommended next
  step. Installs nothing and changes no settings.

## Notes

- Independent community guide. Not affiliated with or endorsed by FreeX, Apple, or any printer
  manufacturer. No proprietary drivers, firmware, or binaries are distributed here.
- All IP addresses and network names in the documentation are placeholders
  (`192.168.1.100`, `YOUR_WIFI_NAME`, `YOUR_MAC_USERNAME`).
